problems.reason: Sentences 17 and 18 repeat the same information about David Hone’s change of opinion on the age of the holotype.
Both sentences state that a second juvenile specimen proved an elongated tail was present, not as long as the falsified tail of the holotype, measuring about 85% of the femur length.

Sentences 25 and 26 date the holotype to ~124.5–124.6 Ma (Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation), while sentence 27 suggests the holotype may actually come from Middle Jurassic deposits, directly contradicting the earlier age assignment.
Sentence 9 states the preserved tail length is only five centimeters, while sentence 11 claims a second juvenile specimen had a tail about 85% of the femur length, implying a much longer tail.
Sentence 19 classifies Dendrorhynchoides as an anurognathid pterosaur, whereas sentence 20 says the original authors classified it as a long‑tailed rhamphorhynchid.
Sentence 21 places Dendrorhynchoides within the subfamily Anurognathinae, while sentence 22 identifies it as sister to a clade of Asiaticognathidae, which is incompatible.
Sentence 27 reports the holotype might be Middle Jurassic, whereas sentence 28 says the author reversed this view and placed it in the Early Cretaceous.

Sentence 29 states the fossil range spans Middle Jurassic to Early Cretaceous, but sentence 30 lists only the Yixian (Early Cretaceous) and Tiaojishan (Middle Jurassic) formations, implying a narrower range.
Both sentences provide the same information that the type species is from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation in Liaoning.
Both sentences describe the holotype GMV2128 as discovered around 1995 and obtained by illegal fossil dealers.
All three sentences describe the inferred lifestyle of Dendrorhynchoides as arboreal insectivorous.
The phrase “part of this is attributed to a section likely added to increase the fossil’s value” refers to an unspecified section of the tail, but no prior mention of such a section exists.
